items.heading: Compared with Architecture, Engineering,
items.text: Compared with architecture, engineering, or most licensed professions, this question carries a different set of trade-offs that families rarely weigh together: almost no legal barrier to entry, a much shorter and cheaper training path, but also a much more crowded, unregulated market where the title alone proves nothing to a client.

items.heading: Before Comparing Pay or Specialisations,
items.text: Before comparing pay or specialisations, it helps to see the actual daily texture of the work, not the version that shows up in a college brochure or an Instagram reel.

rows: 6 months to 2 years, open after Class 10 or Class 12 Direct admission at most private institutes; no national design entrance exam required at most colleges

The fastest, cheapest way into a junior design role or an assistant seat at a modular firm like Livspace or HomeLane. Fees range from a few thousand rupees to several lakh depending on the institute, with almost no correlation between fee and actual placement quality below the well-known names.
4 years, after Class 12 in any stream (science-with-maths preferred by some institutes) NID DAT, NIFT entrance exam, UCEED, or CUET depending on the institute; CEED for postgraduate entry

A genuine national-level entrance filter, a broader design foundation (materials, ergonomics, sustainability, digital tools), and stronger recognition at large firms, developers, and hospitality chains. No NATA-style exam and no equivalent of a mandatory five-year licensing internship exist for this route.

items.heading: Anyone Can Legally Call Themselves
items.text: Anyone can legally call themselves an "interior designer" and take paying clients the moment they choose to, diploma or no diploma; there is no Architects Act-style law protecting the title.

items.heading: Turnkey Platforms Like Livspace
items.text: Turnkey platforms like Livspace and HomeLane have created an entirely new employment model in the last decade, supplying steady client leads to designers who could never have built that pipeline alone.

items.heading: At the Same Time, That
items.text: At the same time, that low barrier to entry means the residential design lane is genuinely crowded and price-competitive, and AI rendering tools are compressing the exact visualisation tasks most junior designers used to build a portfolio on.
